dossier_meta.catalog_title: Informal conjecture on non-tightness of upper bound for binary focal families
dossier_meta.statement_text: For $q = 2$ and large $n$, the upper bound $g^{q\text{-ff}}_r(n) \leq (r-1)\, q^{\lceil (r-2)n/(r-1) \rceil}$ of Theorem 1.3 is not tight.
dossier_meta.context_text: Proposition 3.2 shows via Reed-Solomon codes that the upper bound is essentially tight when $q \geq n$ and $q$ is a prime power. The authors believe the binary case ($q = 2$) behaves differently, and support this belief by proving in Section 4 that the bound can be significantly improved when the family of binary vectors forms a linear code (closed under addition modulo 2).
